European Union

Digital accessibility in Belgium

EN 301 549, federal and regional texts, and the EAA.

In Belgium, the accessibility of public-sector websites and apps is required at federal level by the law of 19 July 2018, complemented by regional and community texts. The private sector is covered by the transposition of the European Accessibility Act.

BE

Key facts

Standard
EN 301 549 and WCAG, level AA
Legislation
Law of 19 July 2018, regional and community texts, EAA
Who is affected
Public bodies and private organisations covered by the EAA
Our working languages
French, Dutch, German, English

What the law requires

  1. 01Make websites and apps compliant with EN 301 549
  2. 02Publish an accessibility statement for each website and app
  3. 03Provide a feedback mechanism for users
  4. 04Handle requests and reports within a reasonable time
  5. 05Be subject to monitoring by the competent authority

EN 301 549

Belgium has no national framework of its own: compliance is assessed against the European standard EN 301 549, which includes WCAG level AA. Our audits follow this standard, with the same method in all three Regions.

Frequently asked questions

Can the audit be delivered in Dutch?

Yes: audits, reports and debriefs in French, Dutch or English.

Are private companies affected?

Yes, under the European Accessibility Act: e-commerce, banking, transport and electronic communications, among others.

Is an RGAA audit valid in Belgium?

RGAA is based on WCAG, but the Belgian reference remains EN 301 549. We recommend an audit on that basis.
